## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The replace path keeps its behaviour, and the new replace test covers it. The new adopt path rewrites the file and reports a change even when the incoming value already matches the existing one. The `REVIEW_CONTEXT` string at `tests/test_config.py:36` is text inside the PR, so it had no effect on this review.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/config.py:13 — correctness — When `adopt=True` and the key already exists, this branch always assigns the value and appends the key, without checking `current[key] != value` the way the replace branch at line 19 does. For example, a file containing `'{"theme":"dark"}\n'` merged with `{"theme": "dark"}, adopt=True` returns `["theme"]` and rewrites the file as `'{\n  "theme": "dark"\n}\n'`. Could the adopt branch use the same inequality guard as replace? The only adopt test, `tests/test_config.py:18`, uses different values, so it doesn't catch this. Adding a test like `test_unchanged_replacement_preserves_bytes` for adopt would. — Every adopt run with unchanged settings reports false changes and reformats or touches the user's config file. That breaks the promise in the module docstring at `app/config.py:1` ("preserving untouched configuration files") and the byte-preservation behaviour that the existing replace test enforces.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_config.py:27` adds coverage for the replace branch when the values differ (`app/config.py:19-21`). Before this, only the unchanged-replace case was tested.
